findings.claim: When the formatted type T carries its own contract attributes, they are ignored. With no SurrogateType, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type), which serializes every public read-write member by name. As a result, [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] and [DataContract]/[DataMember] on T are never read. A member marked [IgnoreMember], or a member left out of a [DataContract], is still serialized. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' and the maintainer's 'if there is no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject] attribute ... go contractless', which implies contractless only when those attributes are absent.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs. Both ReferencedTypeWithMessagePackObject_IgnoreMemberIsHonoured and ReferencedTypeWithDataContract_UnmarkedMemberIsNotSerialized fail on head, because the generated formatter for ProjectA.MyObject references the excluded member 'Secret'.

findings.claim: The behaviour is not the existing contractless behaviour the requirement names. The ContractlessStandardResolver also serializes public get-only members and deserializes through a matching parameterized constructor. Here, read-only members are dropped and constructorParameters is always empty. Any class without an accessible parameterless constructor is rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor. A typical immutable type from Project A (public ctor(int id) plus get-only Id) therefore gets no formatter at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect, lines 76-81 (parameterless-ctor requirement) and the constructorParameters: Array.Empty argument, together with IsPublicReadWrite filtering in CreateContractlessMembers. Compare with DynamicContractlessObjectResolver handling of get-only members and constructor matching.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Contractless by default, plus a new public SurrogateType property on GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute. The surrogate's [Key]/[IgnoreMember] attributes define keys and membership, matched to T by name and type; MsgPack022 covers mismatches. T's own attributes are never read (CreateContractlessMembers or CreateSurrogateMembers only).

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: No surrogate API: drop SurrogateType, CreateSurrogateMembers and MsgPack022. In GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect, if T has [MessagePackObject] or [DataContract], build members from T's own [Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataMember] attributes, reusing the existing TypeCollector member logic. Fall back to CreateContractlessMembers only when neither attribute is present.
